title: Gilman-DAAD Germany Scholarships
summary: DAAD provides up to 40 additional scholarships per year for U.S. undergraduate Pell Grant recipients to study, intern, or take short courses in Germany.

degree_levels.notes: For U.S. undergraduate students (Bachelor's or community college students transferring to a Bachelor's program), or short-term courses/internships.

subject_areas.notes: All disciplines are eligible as part of the eligible study/internship programs.

institutions.notes: German universities or pre-approved summer courses/partner institutions.

residence.notes: Applicants must be living in and applying from the United States of America.

mandatory.text: Must meet all eligibility requirements for a regular Gilman Scholarship
Must be matriculated full-time in a degree program in a U.S. accredited college or university and still be matriculated upon completion
Must have completed their second year of study at the time of departure (or demonstrate transfer into a four-year Bachelor's degree from a community college)
Only U.S. Pell Grant recipients are eligible

exceptions.text: Students who have received a Gilman Scholarship funded by ECA in the past or who are receiving Gilman funding at the time of application are not eligible

funding.description: Funding of up to USD $5,000 depending on each scholar's financial need (determined by IIE). Also includes health, accident, and private liability insurance, and a meeting for scholarship holders in Germany.
funding.duration: 1 – 12 months (Summer or winter short-term course up to three months; semester or academic year; or internships at least 6 weeks in length)

application_rounds.notes: Application announced twice a year in mid-January and mid-August at gilmanscholarship.org, with deadlines in March and October.

recurring_deadline_notes: Announced twice a year in mid-January and mid-August, with deadlines in March and October.

steps.text: Visit the official Gilman website to apply.

sources.title: Gilman-DAAD Germany Scholarships - DAAD - Deutscher Akademischer Austauschdienst
sources.notes: The scholarship funds U.S. undergraduate students to study, intern, or take short courses physically in Germany.
